chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said:
When there are three people in a room, two of them should not whisper (to each other) to the exclusion of the third, for that is what saddens him.

key_terms.يَغُمُّهُ: it saddens him / causes him grief

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette regarding whispering among three people?
ai.summary: In al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes a foundational principle of social etiquette (*adab*) emphasizing emotional sensitivity in group dynamics. It warns that whispering (*tanajji*) creates a sense of exclusion and hiddenness, which can breed suspicion or melancholy (*ghum*) in the third party, thereby disrupting communal harmony. This teaching is often cited by Shia jurists and ethicists to illustrate the importance of transparency and inclusivity in interpersonal relationships.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> having said:
‘When there were three in a room, so two of them should not whisper (to each other) because it would sadden him’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Ali from Yunus ibn Ya’qub from abu al-Hassan, the first (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Out of three people in one house, two of them should not hold a private conversation because it saddens the third.”
